item.title: Fijiana 7s fine-tune preparations ahead of Dubai 7s
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 23/11/2026 The Fiji Airways Fijiana 7s side are fine-tuning their preparations ahead of the HSBC SVNS Dubai 7s this weekend.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 23/11/2026

The Fiji Airways Fijiana 7s side are fine-tuning their preparations ahead of the HSBC SVNS Dubai 7s this weekend.

The side is focusing on strength, recovery and team spirit as the players look forward to another challenging tournament.

The team hit the gym shortly after arriving in Dubai, and their focus remains on the upcoming tournament.

Last year, the side finished fourth at the Dubai 7s after losing 22-12 to Japan.

The Fijiana will kick off their campaign against Canada at 6.44pm on Saturday. They will then take on Japan at 11.44pm before playing New Zealand at 2.52am on Sunday in their final pool match.

The women's semi-finals will begin at 9.12pm on Sunday, while the final is scheduled for 3.35am next Monday.

Meanwhile, the Fiji Men's 7s team will meet New Zealand in their first pool match at 8.36pm on Saturday. They will then take on France at 11.17pm before facing Spain at 4am on Sunday in their final pool match.

The men's semi-finals will kick off at 10.06pm on Sunday, while the final is scheduled for 4.11am next Monday.

item.title: Tailevu focuses on controlling the controllables ahead of Farebrother challenge
item.description: Tailevu captain Eparama Sailo says the team is focused on controlling what they can as they prepare to challenge defending champions Nadroga for the Inkk Farebrother Trophy this Saturday. Sailo acknowledges that beating Nadroga on their home ground will not be easy, but says the team has been reviewing their previous matches and working to address their weaknesses ahead of the challenge.
item.content:encoded:
Tailevu captain Eparama Sailo says the team is focused on controlling what they can as they prepare to challenge defending champions Nadroga for the Inkk Farebrother Trophy this Saturday.

Sailo acknowledges that beating Nadroga on their home ground will not be easy, but says the team has been reviewing their previous matches and working to address their weaknesses ahead of the challenge.

He says Tailevu's focus is on tightening up their set pieces, improving their overall performance and controlling the aspects of the game within their reach to ensure a strong finish.

The Tailevu team has left today for Lautoka and the players are all in good spirit.

Tailevu faces Nadroga this Saturday at Churchill Park, Lautoka, at 3pm.
